payload.description_html: (A, B) Varanus ornatus (Daudin, 1803) ZFMK 14889. (C, D) Varanus komodoensis Ouwens, 1912 ZFMK 64998. (E, F) Varanus griseus (Daudin, 1803) SMF 32911. (G, H) Varanus bengalensis (Daudin, 1802) SMF 63456. Note in all cases the absence of a lateral sulcus along the edge of the narial aperture. In V. ornatus and V. komodoensis there is no hint of medial expansion of the medial edge of the maxilla (no medial concavity along the medial edge of the maxilla in dorsal view), whereas in V. griseus and V. bengalensis a sort of expansion is mostly located in the area anterior to the facial process (presence of a variably developed concavity). Among the four species here depicted, V. ornatus is the only one that bears blunt, molariform teeth.
